direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale builds the world as cheap slapstick, teen comedy that tries to copy the original film; The stunt and martial arts choreography is good and the only reason to watch this movie; The direction on a microscale is atrocious as all the interpersonal scenes feel forced and toneless; The storytelling is so bland and formulaic as they try to follow the original movie's template, but overcomplicate things as the first third of the movie is a carbon copy of the first movie, the middle third is this useless plot line that deviates from the main story, and the final third is them trying to play catch up and rush the entire second half of the original film in 30 minutes; The build-up of tension is poor

performance.comments: Plays a toned-down version of his character in the remake, but has his Jackie Chan charm that makes his scenes enjoyable

Plays the stereotypical teen drama kid who gets bullied and fights his way to the top, but not in a good way; His performance barely has any depth or emotion, but that's mainly because of the direction and writing; Also, this dude is like 25 playing a 16-year-old
Literally plays the "Hello, every pizza place" character from that Family Guy cutaway
Plays the stereotypical teen girl you would see in a teen comedy;  Has some range but nothing great; Forced chemistry with the cast but not terrible
Feels like they gave her character no emotions or material to work with; It does not have good chemistry with Wang as they barely give her any time to develop a mother-son relationship
What are you doing in this movie; They like to force his presence on screen and act like he's the protagonist's best friend; But there are no scenes between the two besides them tutoring
Literally a stoic bully with no emotions or screen time

They straight up forgot this dude was supposed to be in this movie because he shows up with thirty minutes left;  He basically plays a continuation of his Cobra Kai character but with worse material and less range; He has good chemistry with Chan which makes me wonder why they didn't use this dynamic more in the movie because it's literally forced in the last thirty minutes

cast.comments: The most inexperienced, bad teen movie acting you can get, as the performances feel forced and do nothing to move the story forward; This does not include child actors, but given that the kids in the main cast are in their 20s, I doubt there were any actual kids in this movie

story.comments: The concept is literally the same movie as the original, but worse in every way; The plot structure is a complete mess because the first third of the movie is literally exactly the same as the first movie, the middle third they try something different by making the Karate Kid Mr. Miyagi, but then they go back to the original template in the final third and cram the entire second half of the original movie into 30 minutes; The character writing is terrible because all of these characters are shallow stereotypes of the original movie and generic teen comedies, and they do not even do anything with Han and LaRusso, which is crazy because they could have done fan service for the latter

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is so bad because they basically made this movie a terrible slapstick teen comedy; The humor is so forced and never hits, except for the post-credit scene; The symbolism is the exact same as the original movie; The foreshadowing is present but it is also mainly because they use the exact same template as the first movie

score.comments: Barely interpolates the original themes; Decent, besides the bare minimum they could have done to make it interesting

cinematography.comments: The cinematography during the martial arts sequences is actually entertaining; but besides that, it is decent throughout; but it has some weird shots in the final 30 minutes

editing.comments: The slideshow edits were some of the cheapest cuts I have ever seen; The movie has these weird TikTok edits toward the end, which makes me believe they tried to make this movie for Gen Z

visual_effects.comments: Pretty fake when they use visual effects, but the movie is mostly practical effects and martial arts sequences

production_design.comments: These weird, fake, constructed sets mimicked Manhattan; the Miyagi house was a nice set

review.pacing: Pacing is not really an issue; the movie just feels slow because of the poorly constructed plot
review.climax: Climax is so fast and forced that it barely even happens; it's literally the exact same ending as the original movie
review.tone: The tone is slapstick, teen comedy
review.final_notes: They straight-up forgot Cobra Kai was the reason Karate Kid is relevant again; They remember the show at the end, but by the time they reference it, it is too late
review.overall: Overall, a very bad movie that literally tries to recreate the original movie, but is worse in every way as it ended up being this cheap, slapstick teen comedy with no substance; The movie can't even do fan service correctly because they straight up forget to put Daniel LaRusso until the very end and barely mention Cobra Kai at all
